hypotheses.justification: The theorem pulls this instance in automatically, because every variable its type mentions is already an argument. The statement `Module.Finite (ZMod p) (↥P0 →+ ZMod p)` does not need it to elaborate. The only place it is used is in the local instance `moduleFinite_P0`, through `P0.restrictScalars ℤ_[p]`. But it can be derived from the other hypotheses. Let T = TateModule p (JH M H). By `ModularCurve.moduleFinite_and_free_padicInt_tateModule_jH M p H`, which only needs `[NeZero M] [Fact p.Prime]`, T is a finite free ℤ_[p]-module, so the intersection of the p^k • T over all k is 0. Take c ∈ ℤ_[p] and x ∈ T. For each k, write c = n + p^k·b with n ∈ ℕ; this is the same kind of decomposition (`exists_eq_natCast_add_mul`) used in `moduleFinite_hom` in this file. Since `algebraMap ℤ_[p] 𝕋` is a ring hom, it sends n to n and p^k to p^k. So (algebraMap c) • x − c • x = p^k • ((algebraMap b) • x − b • x), which lies in p^k • T for every k and is therefore 0. Hence algebraMap c • x = c • x, and (c • t) • x = (algebraMap c * t) • x = algebraMap c • (t • x) = c • (t • x). That is the `IsScalarTower` instance. With it rebuilt locally, the existing proof goes through unchanged: P0 is a ℤ_[p]-submodule of the finite module T over the Noetherian ring ℤ_[p], so it is finite, and `moduleFinite_hom p ↥P0` concludes. No degenerate case causes trouble: if T = 0, everything is trivially finite.
